messages:
alex: Idea: a 'throttle reservoir' concept for smoothing tenant bursts. not per-tenant-only baskets but a tiny shared reservoir that can be loaned for short spikes. thoughts on API boundaries?
rucha: Interesting. how is this different from existing provisional credits or soft-credits?
alex: two differences: (1) reservoir is short-lived pooled credit (seconds->minutes), not long-term quota; (2) it exposes a simple contract to admission/frontdoor: request n tokens, response: granted=(n|partial|0), source=(own|reservoir). keeps enforcement centralized.
dave: source tag is useful for telemetry. perf concern: could add contention in admission path if we hit reservoir atomic ops. prefer optimistic local counters with periodic reconciliation.
morgan: agree about local fastpath. maybe admission returns a small lease token when it hands out reservoir credit: lease={amount, expiry, id}. proxies can spend lease without re-querying until expiry.
alex: exactly. wire idea: header: X-RW-Lease: id=abc;amt=40;exp=171234; and admission still returns admission_state and rep_score.
rucha: abuse signal integration? we should prevent reservoir from subsidizing abusive clients. propose reservoir eligibility based on rep_score < threshold and recent false_positive flag. also cap per-tenant reservoir draw over sliding window.
dave: telemetry: reservoir_usage_total, reservoir_loans_by_tenant, loan_expiry_misses, loans_revoked. also record loan_source so we can backfill chargeback when we reconcile.
morgan: fallback routing: if loan_source==reservoir, routing-service may prefer cheaper model to reduce cost. but that must be opt-in mapping to avoid silent regressions.
alex: admin tools: console should show active loans, allow manual reclaim for emergency, and an operator API POST /admin/reservoir/reclaim?tenant=.. with explanation param. all actions go to audit log.
rucha: testing: synthetic harness with bursty tenants that would have hit soft-warns. measure p95 latency and loan exhaustion curves. define KPIs: loan_hit_rate, loan_helped_success_rate, and loan_abuse_rate.
dave: correctness: lease revocation path must be robust: when reputation flips mid-lease we should let lease expire but mark tenant for next-not-granted. revocation only for severe safety.
morgan: implementation owners: admission service owns scoring + loans, proxy/runtime owns lease caching + spend semantics, platform owns console + overrides.
alex: rollout: phase 1 shadow mode where admission returns loans but proxies ignore. collect shadow metrics 2w. phase 2: opt-in enforcement for a handful of tenants. phase 3: gradual auto-opt for noisy patterns.
deploy-bot: scheduling: reservoir shadow rollout to infra-shadow at 2026-06-07T08:00Z (CI #9901).
rucha: one more tradeoff: reservoir increases complexity in billing attribution. we must ensure chargeback is deterministic: when loan is used, attribute tokens to original tenant; if reclaimed, attribute to reservoir edge pool and bill to platform cost center.
dave: add deterministic ledger events: LOAN_GRANTED, LOAN_USED, LOAN_RECLAIMED. stream to events topic for reconciliation.
morgan: ok. i'll draft a compact RFC with wire headers, lease example, and a small state machine for loans. pairing session tomorrow 11:00am to align on caches. thanks. :thumbsup:
